title: Arnaud Costinot, MIT 14.54: Lecture 4, Exchange Economies (Fall 2016)
use: Method route for fixed-endowment economies, relative prices, trade and simultaneous market consistency; endowment-sensitive aggregate demand when preferences differ.
verification: Retrieved the actual 35-page official course PDF through the course's lecture-4 resource and read the text of slides 6 and 18–34. Inspected the distinction between fixed resources and demand responses, common relative prices, interacting demands, and the explicit endowment dependence when preferences differ. Source graphs attributed to another author were not reused. The chapter's two-consumer data, coordinate table, wealth accounting, Walras-law algebra, contract curve and all numerical examples are original. No empirical trade-speed, currency-exchange or representative-consumer claim is imported from adjacent source sections.

title: Robert M. Townsend, MIT 14.04: Lecture 16, Fundamental Welfare Theorems (Fall 2020), official transcript
use: Primary lecture content on the finite first-theorem value proof, smooth supporting-price and wealth-transfer construction, and the weaker consumer condition in price quasiequilibrium.
verification: Retrieved the actual 14-page official transcript. Inspected pages 2–4 on weakly preferred bundle costs, LNS, firm profit maximization and the feasibility contradiction; pages 5–10 on smooth planner/consumer/firm conditions and ownership-consistent transfers; and pages 11–12 on the quasiequilibrium inequality and convex separation route. The manuscript states its finite-dimensional assumptions explicitly, proves only its restricted constructive decentralization result and cheaper-bundle upgrade, and does not claim the general separation theorem or graduate infinite-dimensional proof has been supplied. The source's verbal slips and loose equivalence between utility concavity and preference regularity are not adopted. No source empirical illustration or exercise is copied.

title: Robert M. Townsend, MIT 14.04: Lecture 20, Failure of Welfare Theorems (Fall 2020), official transcript
use: Method scope for nonconvex support failures, local satiation and pollution omitted from private commodity prices; distinction between price-taking private choices and the larger feasible welfare comparison.
verification: Retrieved the actual 14-page official transcript and inspected pages 3–8, including its self-correction about failure of the second rather than first welfare theorem, local-satiation example, signed-input production notation, missing pollution price and private household/firm optimization. The chapter independently builds and solves a two-household production/pollution economy, an explicit compensated Pareto improvement and a nonconvex technology counterexample. It does not copy the lecture's numerical setup, treat mere nonconvexity as certain failure, or claim a pollution instrument has been implemented. Cryptocurrency, platform and infinite-horizon sections were outside the cited scope.
